es: Clasificar errores frecuentes del nivel por categoría, reconocer qué regla se ha roto en cada uno y decidir cuáles son recurrentes y cuáles simples descuidos.

vocabulary.es: punto ciego, laguna que no ves
error fosilizado (hábito que ya no se corrige)

teaching.en: To diagnose a mistake properly, name its category and look for the root cause before you touch the sentence.
teaching.es: Para diagnosticar bien un error, nombra su categoría y busca la causa de fondo antes de tocar la frase.
teaching.explanationEs: Primero la categoría (gramática oral, concesión, tacto, registro, narración) y después la regla rota: así la corrección se queda contigo.
segments: To diagnose a mistake properly, name its category and look
for the root cause before you touch the sentence.
teaching.audioText: To diagnose a mistake properly, name its category and look for the root cause before you touch the sentence.

teaching.en: A careless slip is a one-off, but a recurring error points to a blind spot, a rule you have never fully absorbed.
teaching.es: Un desliz por descuido ocurre una sola vez, pero un error recurrente señala una laguna, una regla que nunca has interiorizado del todo.
teaching.explanationEs: Cuenta cuántas veces aparece el mismo fallo: si se repite, ya no es descuido, es una laguna.
segments: A careless slip is a one-off, but a recurring error points
to a blind spot, a rule you have never fully absorbed.
teaching.audioText: A careless slip is a one-off, but a recurring error points to a blind spot, a rule you have never fully absorbed.

teaching.en: To pinpoint a spoken-grammar slip, check the pronoun: That film, it was brilliant sounds natural, but That film, was brilliant does not.
teaching.es: Para localizar un desliz de gramática oral, revisa el pronombre: That film, it was brilliant suena natural, pero That film, was brilliant no.
teaching.explanationEs: La cabeza (That film) se retoma con un pronombre; en español no hace falta, y de ahí viene el fallo.
segments: To pinpoint a spoken-grammar slip, check the pronoun: That film, it
was brilliant sounds natural, but That film, was brilliant does not.
teaching.audioText: To pinpoint a spoken-grammar slip, check the pronoun: That film, it was brilliant sounds natural, but That film, was brilliant does not.

teaching.en: Within the concession category, much as already carries the contrast, so a following but is redundant: Much as I admire her, I disagree.
teaching.es: Dentro de la categoría de la concesión, much as ya lleva el contraste, así que un but posterior sobra: Much as I admire her, I disagree.
teaching.explanationEs: Añadir but es un calco de «aunque… pero»; en inglés much as basta.
segments: Within the concession category, much as already carries the contrast, so a
following but is redundant: Much as I admire her, I disagree.
teaching.audioText: Within the concession category, much as already carries the contrast, so a following but is redundant: Much as I admire her, I disagree.

teaching.en: Academic register prefers a noun to a verb, so prices fell becomes the fall in prices, with in, not of, marking what changed.
teaching.es: El registro académico prefiere un sustantivo a un verbo, así que prices fell pasa a the fall in prices, con in, no of, para lo que cambia.
teaching.explanationEs: Con sustantivos de cambio (increase, drop, growth) lo que cambia se introduce con in.
segments: Academic register prefers a noun to a verb, so prices fell becomes
the fall in prices, with in, not of, marking what changed.
teaching.audioText: Academic register prefers a noun to a verb, so prices fell becomes the fall in prices, with in, not of, marking what changed.

teaching.en: Take stock of each rough draft and spot a pattern: a fossilised error appears as a recurring mark in the margin.
teaching.es: Haz balance de cada borrador preliminar y detecta un patrón: un error fosilizado aparece como una marca recurrente en el margen.
teaching.explanationEs: Un error fosilizado es el que ya sale sin pensar; solo se detecta comparando varios borradores.
segments: Take stock of each rough draft and spot a pattern: a
fossilised error appears as a recurring mark in the margin.

prompt.es: Diagnostica el desliz de este borrador: ¿qué categoría y qué regla fallan?

choices.text: Spoken grammar: the topic needs a pronoun to pick it up.
Concession: much as already contrasts, so but is redundant.
Academic register: a noun should replace the verb here.

feedback.es: Much as ya expresa el contraste, así que el but posterior sobra: es un desliz de concesión; la frase no tiene cabeza sin pronombre ni verbo que nominalizar.

hint.es: Fíjate en el conector que sobra detrás de la primera parte de la frase.

origin.text: Much as I like the idea, but it costs far too much, and no sponsor has come forward.

prompt.es: Completa: «No es un desliz, sino un error recurrente que debe diagnosticar.»

feedback.es: Un error que reaparece en todos los borradores es recurrente: a diferencia del descuido, señala una regla no asimilada.

hint.es: Adjetivo que describe un error que vuelve a aparecer una y otra vez.

origin.text: The same mistake appears in all of Ana's drafts. It is not a careless slip but a ___ error, and she has to diagnose it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nombra la categoría antes de tocar la frase.»

answer.text: Name the category before you touch the sentence
accepted: Name the category before you touch the sentence
Before you touch the sentence, name the category

feedback.es: La orden comienza por el diagnóstico (name the category) y deja la corrección para después de la conjunción before.

hint.es: Empieza por el verbo que pide el diagnóstico; before introduce lo que hacer después.

prompt.es: Según estas marcas, ¿qué error de Tom es recurrente y de qué categoría?

choices.text: Of after a noun of change, a register slip that keeps coming back.
A missing full stop, a careless slip that is easy to fix and need not worry him.
A wrong date, a slip that spoils the order of events.
Missing pronouns, a spoken-grammar slip that appears in most drafts.

feedback.es: Increase of, rise of y fall of repiten la misma preposición tras un sustantivo de cambio: es un error de registro recurrente; el punto y la fecha aparecen una sola vez.

origin.text: Tutor's marks on Tom's drafts. Draft one: the increase of sales. Draft two: the rise of costs, and one missing full stop. Draft three: the fall of prices. Draft four: a wrong date.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige qué conclusión saca de las marcas de su tutor.

choices.text: Her mistakes are spread across several categories instead of falling into one.
Her corrections show that verbs are the one real weakness she must study.
The four corrections are too few to show any weakness at all.

feedback.es: Sara observa que cada marca pertenece a una categoría distinta; por eso no hay una única debilidad a la que culpar.

origin.audio: Sara reads the notes her tutor left on her draft. The first two corrections change a verb, the third fixes the tense of a story told in the past, and the last softens a request. Sara sighs and realises that every mark belongs to a different category, so there is no single weakness to blame.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con error con la regla que rompe.

pairs.es: Gramática oral: falta el pronombre que retoma el tema

I wonder where is the manager

pairs.es: Tacto: la pregunta indirecta no invierte el orden

pairs: The growth of sales slowed down

pairs.es: Registro: lo que cambia se introduce con in

pairs: When Sara arrived, the speaker already left

pairs.es: Narración: lo anterior pide had + participio

feedback.es: Cada frase rompe una regla distinta: el pronombre del tema, el contraste, el orden de la pregunta indirecta, la preposición de cambio y el tiempo de lo anterior (had).

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué da a entender el tutor sobre cómo debería estudiar Mia.

choices.text: She should reread every draft twice to catch the slips before handing it in.
She should drill the increase of prices, which is her only recurring error.
She should put her effort into the repeated errors instead of the slips.
She should ask him to mark fewer slips in her next drafts.

feedback.es: El tutor resta importancia a los descuidos y pide un diagnóstico de los errores recurrentes: eso orienta la prioridad de estudio de Mia.

origin.audio: Mia's tutor has just finished marking her last four drafts. Fourteen marks in total, he says, but only six of them are careless slips: a dropped article here, a missing plural there, the kind of thing Mia corrects herself as soon as she reads them again. The other eight are different. Three times she wrote the increase of prices, twice she added but after much as, and three times she opened a request with a direct question. According to the tutor, nobody should lose sleep over the slips, whereas the recurring errors deserve a proper diagnosis, because they show rules she has never really absorbed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra Tom ante las correcciones que ha recibido?

choices.text: He is grateful, but doubts that the marks describe his real weakness.
He is pleased that the marks confirm what he thought about vocabulary.
He is discouraged and thinks he will never sound natural in writing.
He is surprised, but ready to change his study plan because of the marks.

feedback.es: Tom dice que esperaba un problema de vocabulario y que las marcas cuentan otra historia; empieza un registro de correcciones, lo que revela sorpresa y disposición a cambiar de plan.

origin.text: Hi Ana, thanks for marking my drafts. I had assumed that my main weakness was vocabulary, but the marks tell a different story: nearly all of them concern how I sound rather than what I say. I have started keeping a log of my corrections, and I intend to bring it to our next session in case it helps us decide where to begin.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo la ayudó a rastrear el error hasta su causa de fondo.»

feedback.es: Root cause es la colocación para el origen real de un problema; detrás de la repetición hay una causa, aquí la traducción literal.

origin.text: The same error appeared in every one of Ana's drafts. When Leo helped her trace it back to its ___ cause, she saw that it was a blind spot: she had been copying a Spanish pair of linking words into English word for word.

prompt.es: Diagnostica en inglés: nombra la categoría del error y la regla que rompe.

answer.text: This is a register slip. After a noun of change such as drop, the thing that changes takes in, so the correct phrase is the drop in prices.
accepted: This is a register slip. After a noun of change such as drop, the thing that changes takes in, so the correct phrase is the drop in prices.
It is an academic register error: drop needs in, not of, so we should say the drop in prices.
This is a slip of register. A noun of change like drop is followed by in, so it should be the drop in prices.

feedback.es: Un buen diagnóstico nombra la categoría (registro), enuncia la regla (in tras un sustantivo de cambio) y da la frase corregida.

origin.text: La frase marcada en el borrador de Leo es: «The drop of prices worried the managers.» Explica de qué categoría es el error y cuál es la frase correcta.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Detecta un patrón antes de culpar a un desliz por descuido.»

answer.text: Spot a pattern before you blame a careless slip
accepted: Spot a pattern before you blame a careless slip
Before you blame a careless slip, spot a pattern

feedback.es: El patrón se busca primero: solo cuando el fallo no se repite tiene sentido culpar al descuido.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la autora este párrafo?

choices.text: To argue that repeated mistakes need a named rule, not merely more attention.
To warn learners that careless slips cost more marks than recurring errors.
To reassure learners that repeated marks disappear once they write more.
To describe how one learner improved her writing over a single term.

feedback.es: La autora rechaza la idea de que el problema sea la falta de cuidado y defiende que una regla sin nombre seguirá produciendo la misma marca.

origin.text: Most learners read their corrections and promise to be more careful, which is precisely the wrong lesson. Care is not the issue. A sentence such as the increase of prices worried us is not careless; it simply reflects a rule that was never absorbed. Until that rule has a name, no amount of attention will stop the same mark from returning in the next draft.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se habla de una fuerte caída de los precios.»

feedback.es: El sustantivo de cambio (fall, drop) sustituye al verbo y pide in para lo que cambia: the sharp fall in prices.

origin.text: Academic writers prefer nouns to verbs. Instead of saying that prices fell sharply, they refer to the sharp ___ in prices, and that small change is enough to raise the register of the sentence.
